chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجَ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:

chunks.arabic_text: لَا يُجْبَرُ الرَّجُلُ إِلَّا عَلَى نَفَقَةِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْوَلَدِ، قَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: قُلْتُ لِجَمِيلٍ: وَالْمَرْأَةُ؟ قَالَ: قَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ عِنْبَسَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ: إِذَا كَسَاهَا مَا يُورِي عَوْرَتَهَا وَيُطْعِمُهَا مَا يُقِيمُ صَلْبَهَا أَقَامَتْ مَعَهُ وَإِلَّا طَلَّقَهَا

translations.en: A man is not obliged [to provide maintenance] except for the parents and the children. Ibn Abi Umayr said: I said to Jamil: and what about the wife? He said: It has been narrated from Anbasa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: If he clothes her with what covers her private parts and feeds her with what sustains her strength, she remains with him; otherwise, he divorces her.

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi clarifies the reciprocal financial duties in marriage, specifying that a husband's obligation to provide clothing covering the 'awrah and food sustaining the body is the condition for the wife's right to cohabitation. It highlights the scholarly principle that if these essential provisions cease, the marital bond is effectively dissolved, necessitating divorce, thereby linking material provision directly to the continuity of the marital contract.
en.seo_question: What are the conditions for a wife's right to maintenance and continued marriage according to this hadith?
